key_insight: Drilled-to-bossed geometry improved AA2024-T351 friction-weld strength, while an ensemble residual network predicted ultimate tensile strength with R² ≈ 0.81.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-assisted direct drive friction welding could support stronger joints in lightweight aerospace and automotive aluminium components.
method: Tested five welding parameters using an L18 orthogonal array on a customized engine lathe.
Compared drilled-to-bossed and conventional flat-to-flat faying surfaces through tensile and torsional testing.
Evaluated ensemble residual, compact attention, and adaptive multiscale networks for tensile-strength prediction.
evidence_signal: The reported optimum—30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, and 4 min friction time—achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify independent model validation or experimental replication, leaving predictive generalization and strength variability uncertain.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
